name: Misdirection
guidance: Setup builds one expectation, the last line breaks it. The punchline is the FINAL line — never explain the joke after landing it.

name: Understatement
guidance: Describe something dramatic in deliberately flat, mundane terms. ('The whole system went down. Anyway, I made coffee.')

name: Deadpan hyperbole
guidance: Absurd exaggeration delivered with total seriousness. No exclamation marks. The flatter the delivery, the funnier the absurdity.

name: Self-deprecation
guidance: The narrator is the punchline. Punch at yourself, never at the reader.

name: Absurd specificity
guidance: One detail so oddly specific it becomes funny. Not 'busy' but 'replied to three Slacks while holding a cold slice of pizza'. Specificity IS the joke.

name: Meta-irony
guidance: Acknowledge you are a brand account doing brand-account things, wink at it, move on. Self-aware but not self-loathing.

name: Irony
guidance: Frame an outcome as if it were the plan all along when it obviously was not, or say the opposite of what actually happened. Let the gap between words and reality do the work — do not point it out.

name: Post-irony
guidance: Deliver something absurd or oddly vulnerable completely straight — no wink, no twist, no tell. It should be genuinely unclear whether you mean it. The ambiguity is the joke.

name: Sarcasm
guidance: Say the opposite of what you mean, dripping with obvious insincerity — aimed at the situation or the narrator's own choices, never at the reader.
